steps.body: Now run it in reverse: shown a frame-and-extras picture, NAME the teen. Count the extras, put “ten and” in front, and the numeral appears.
steps.narration: Now run it in reverse: shown a frame-and-extras picture, NAME the teen. Count the extras, put “ten and” in front, and the numeral appears.

widget.prompt: A full group of 10 is already shown. Add the extra dots needed to make 12.

commonCounts.feedback: 0 leaves 2 dots still missing — the ten alone only makes 10, not 12.
1 leaves 1 dot still missing; ten and 1 is 11, one short of 12.
3 adds 1 too many; ten and 3 is 13, one past 12.

widget.missFeedback: The ten is done; count on from 10 while adding dots, and stop when you reach 12.
widget.successFeedback: 12 built — one complete ten and 2 more, exactly what the teen numeral says.

predict.prompt: Full frame, 6 dots outside. Which teen?
predict.reveal: The outsiders ride on a finished ten; the name must carry both parts.

cml.actionGoal: Build one complete ten, then count on the ones, for knb identify teen.
invariants: Every teen number is one complete ten and some ones — the left digit records the finished ten, the right digit counts the extras — and that split is what knb identify teen rests on.
misconceptions: Reading the 1 of a teen as “one” instead of one TEN, or counting only the leftover ones and forgetting the completed ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more dot joined the ones, which teen would the frame show then?

widget.prompt: A frame shows a full ten and 3 outside. Which teen is it?

options.label: 13 — ten and three
options.feedback: Correct — one complete ten and 3 ones is exactly what the numeral 13 records.

options.label: 3 — just the outsiders
options.feedback: Counting only the extras drops the completed ten; the whole group is ten and three.

options.label: 30 — three and a zero
options.feedback: 30 means three TENS; here there is one ten and three ones, which is 13.

options.label: 10 — the frame alone
options.feedback: The frame's ten is only part of the group; the 3 outside push the total to 13.

widget.prompt: A group shows 16 dots. Which numeral names that amount?

options.feedback: Correct — a full ten and 6 more is what the numeral 16 says: 1 ten, 6 ones.
That numeral names one more dot than the group shows.
That numeral stops one dot short; the ten plus the extras reaches 16.
6 counts only the extras and forgets the whole completed ten underneath.

widget.prompt: What number comes right before 18? Hop one back and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 18 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop back to reach 17.
16 goes one complete hop too far. Count exactly 1 hop back from 18 to reach 17.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 back from 18: you land on 17.
widget.successFeedback: 17 — one hop back through the teens, one less than 18.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — one hop back from 18 reaches 17.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right before 18 means a single hop back, stopping on 17.
